headline: Gen Z protests end in riots in Frankfurt and Berlin, a critical Linux TCP bug is still unpatched on Ubuntu and RHEL, and Reeves says the UK belongs in the EU

stories.title: Gen Z protest day ends in riots: shops looted in Frankfurt, 56 arrests in Berlin
facts: After largely peaceful "Gen Z regelt" marches on Saturday, rioters looted shops on Frankfurt's Zeil late in the evening, smashed a gun shop's window and threw molotov cocktails at police.
Frankfurt police detained more than 30 people, sent in the SEK special unit and used water cannon and tear gas; around 1:00 they held a group of about 100 people to check identities.
In Berlin, 3,500 people marched through the centre in the evening; 27 officers were lightly injured and 56 people were arrested.
Köln saw barricades of e-scooters on the Domplatte and water cannon, Hamburg water cannon near the Hauptbahnhof, and Stuttgart about 50 offences with five officers lightly hurt.

Hesse's interior minister Roman Poseck says about 100 identified left-wing extremists infiltrated the Frankfurt march; state premier Boris Rhein says the attackers put themselves "outside our society".
France had its third protest weekend in a row, with more than 320,000 people out and over 500 arrests after clashes.
stories.whyItMatters: Yesterday's story was the turnout; this morning it's the violence, which will shape how politicians answer the movement's demands on schools, living costs and military service.

image.alt: People try to break a window of a store selling weapons, during a nationwide protest by campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen Z takes charge) against underfunding of schools, cuts to education, social services, culture and healthcare, rising living costs, and military conscription, in Frankfurt, Germany.

stories.title: A critical remote bug in Linux's TCP handshake still has no fix on Ubuntu or RHEL
facts: CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake that an unauthenticated remote peer can reach, before any application sees the connection; the kernel scores it CVSS 9.8.
Upstream fixed it on Oct 11 and 15 (5.10.272 up to 7.2.10, and 7.3); the bug goes back to Linux 4.4.
Red Hat raised it to Critical on Oct 30 but has no fixed RHEL 8, 9 or 10 kernel yet, and Ubuntu lists every release as vulnerable; Debian, SUSE, Oracle UEK and Amazon Linux are fixed.
Anthropic, whose researcher reported it, says Claude wrote a working root exploit for servers with a multipath TCP listener, which Go programs open by default since Go 1.24.
Until a kernel ships, the interim fix is an nftables rule dropping TCP packets that carry IPv4 options, or turning MPTCP off; 36 GitHub repos already reference the CVE.
stories.whyItMatters: It sits in code every Linux server runs, and public race triggers are appearing while two of the biggest distributions still have no patch.

image.alt: Linux's October 2026 TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 — Atlas

stories.title: Claude Code now refuses to recreate existing games, and some developers say real work gets caught
facts: Since about Oct 27, a server-delivered Claude Code instruction says: build original and genre games, but "do not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed".
Anthropic's Addy Osmani confirmed two sentences were added to the Opus 5.5 prompt because using Claude to infringe IP breaks its usage policy, and said it will keep tuning the balance.
A board-wargame module developer filed a GitHub issue saying paid client work that ran for months is now refused, and asks for a verification path for professionals.
Tom's Hardware collects further complaints about reverse-engineering tasks being blocked, though a link to the game rule isn't proven.
Separately, researcher Jiahao Shao says Anthropic flagged him for "training a competitor" and now blocks anything touching RFT, SFT or training larger models; the post hit 307 points on Hacker News.
stories.whyItMatters: Studios are scared of AI clones of their demos, but the rule shows how hard it is to block piracy without blocking legitimate builders.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves says Britain's future lies inside the EU
facts: In her first big intervention since leaving the Treasury, the former chancellor wrote in the Sunday Times that Brexit made the UK "poorer, weaker and less secure".
"I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union," she wrote, adding that rejoiners must show tangible benefits.
She wants the coming UK-EU summit to confirm a youth mobility scheme and progress towards joining the EU's SAFE defence fund.
Labour's 2024 manifesto ruled out the single market, customs union and free movement; Prime Minister Andy Burnham says any change would need a mandate at an election due by 2029.
The Conservatives and Reform UK's Nigel Farage reject reopening the Brexit debate.
stories.whyItMatters: A former chancellor saying "rejoin" out loud moves the Labour debate on Europe ahead of next month's Brussels summit.

image.alt: Rachel Reeves makes a speech at the annual Financial and Professional Services Dinner at Mansion House in London.

facts.text: The FBI officially blames North Korea's TraderTraitor for the $6.3bn Binance theft and expects the funds to be laundered further; Binance says it has already replaced 90% of the stolen assets.
A public exploit for Android's "SMS of Death" (CVE-2026-58882) crashes the phone service with an invisible text, dropping even emergency calls; Android 12 and 13 stay unpatched.
A judge threw out Trump's $10bn suit against the Wall Street Journal over the Epstein birthday letter "with prejudice", so it can't be refiled.
IG Metall's warning strikes started at midnight in Andernach and München; the union chief says the employers' offer caused "incomprehension and anger".
Lewis Hamilton took his first pole for Ferrari in Mexico, 0.009s ahead of George Russell, with Leclerc third; the race is tonight.
An EA office in Madrid was sprayed with "Save Mass Effect" days after EA shut down BioWare, IGN reports.

facts.text: Karpathy built HackerTube, a YouTube front end for 6,454 videos recommended in about 40,000 Hacker News comments since 2007; he says it took about two hours with Opus 5.5 on medium effort.
Jarred Sumner says Bun's ahead-of-time mode cuts memory by 40% and CPU by 14% in an Express plus node:sqlite REST API, with no JIT warmup; Bun also merged bun test --aot for large suites.
Epic Games published an Unreal Engine skills plugin for Claude Code.
Vercel CI is in public beta, switched on with one line in turbo.json; Vercel says it is 2 to 6 times faster than its previous CI in its own repos.
KDE introduced Kwi, a new terminal emulator.
matklad argues public functions shouldn't call other public functions.

facts.text: The AI Corner on building your own AI legal team with Claude skills.
Bayern 2:2 BVB: Guirassy equalised in the 60th minute and sub Fábio Silva in the 89th; Kane hit the bar with a penalty. Both teams have 18 points, Bayern top on goal difference.
Kimmich, back as Bayern captain after his father's sudden death, said returning was hard because on the pitch is when he thinks of him most.
Basketball Löwen Braunschweig lost 72:96 at home to Würzburg.
The Golden State Valkyries, the Warriors' WNBA sister team, beat the Atlanta Dream 68–63 in Game 7 for their first title, the fastest an expansion team has won the WNBA.
The Warriors play the Clippers on Nov 1, and two 49ers players were fined for incidents in the loss to the Falcons.
